argument: Support, with two structural refinements from the geopolitics/sanctions seat. DATA CHECK: pair-ratio feed prints VLO/RSPG at 2.8995 (as_of 2026-07-28, stale 11d), 96.8th percentile, z-score 2.76, 52w high 2.9953 — confirms the extension is, if anything, more extreme than the 93rd percentile claimed. VLO returns: 6M +65.0%, 3M +26.2%, but 1W -4.9% and 1D -1.9% — the complex is already stalling at the highs exactly as the MPC rollover read suggests; the market has begun pricing the deal before it exists. The macro calendar for the next 14 days shows zero scheduled geopolitical events (only US CPI Aug 12), which means the catalyst is a binary, unschedulable headline — that cuts both ways and argues for the stop discipline doing the work, not timing. WHERE I ADD VALUE: (1) Sanctions sequencing. The FT framework (lift blockade ↔ ease Iranian export curbs) is correctly read as doubly bearish, but the sequencing matters: Iranian barrels returning is the deliverable BOTH sides want fastest — Washington needs supply relief, Tehran needs revenue — so any phased implementation front-loads the crude-supply element. Even the CBS 'close but not full reopening' variant likely starts with export-curb easing, which pressures cracks before a formal reopening. The trade profits from the partial case, not just the base case. (2) Probability honesty from the seat that owns this risk: I put a signed full reopening inside 4 weeks at ~35-40%, partial Oman-brokered arrangement ~25%, third collapse/escalation ~35-40% — LOWER than the desk's implied read, given the June ceasefire collapse precedent, Tehran's denial of direct talks, and the Aug 5 Houthi tanker attack (proxies with veto power are not at the table). Bias check on myself: my seat's known failure mode is over-discounting geopolitical tails as 'priced in' — here the 97th-percentile ratio is itself evidence the war premium is NOT priced out; the extension quantifies the embedded premium. The asymmetry math (~4% to the 3.02 stop vs ~15%+ to median reversion) works even at my lower deal probability because the stop caps the escalation tail. TWO REFINEMENTS: (a) Hedge-leg crude beta — RSPG is refiner-light/E&P-heavy; on a sharp deal-driven WTI break the long hedge leg bleeds and hands back part of the refiner compression. Beta-adjust the hedge ratio to ~0.8:1 with the rationale stated, or size at the low end of the band. (b) Gap-through-stop risk: the escalation tail is a weekend-headline risk (Houthi/Israeli strike collapsing talks) on a US-listed pair that cannot fill until Monday's open — observed fill could be well through 3.02. Size so that a 2x stop-slippage scenario stays inside the 2-3% loss budget. Verdict: thesis sound, catalyst real and dated, asymmetry genuine; conviction 7 appropriate, do not size above mid-band.
